tests.comment: Mutate first, so the undo below has something of the tool's own making to reverse.

'All mutations support Ctrl+Z' is a headline README claim that nothing asserted. It is driven through execute_script because EditorUndoRedoManager — what EditorPlugin.get_undo_redo() hands the tools — exposes no undo() to scripting at all; only get_history_undo_redo(), which returns the plain UndoRedo that does. The action name is asserted too: it proves the mutation was committed as a named editor action rather than merely reversed by hand, which is what makes it a Ctrl+Z away in the editor's own menu.
Undoing a creation has to remove the node from the tree, not merely forget it.
Redo is the other half: a tool that registers only the undo leg leaves the editor unable to put the change back, and nothing else in the suite exercises the do leg a second time.

Not a node tool: add_audio_player goes through _add_to_scene on the 9.3 base class, which is the single commit path behind 13 add_* tools across audio, physics, particles, navigation and scene-3d. One undo here covers all of them; the node tools commit their own actions separately.
Keeper is the first child, deliberately: undoing a delete has to put the node back where it was, and re-adding it is the easy half that a naive undo gets right while appending it last.

Reparenting has the most undo operations of any node tool, so it is where an ordering mistake does the most damage. It also lands here on purpose: committing an action after UR-09's undo discards the redo branch, which is where delete_node registered its do-reference to Keeper — if that reference frees a node the undo just put back in the tree, Keeper stops resolving right here.

Undoing a move has to detach from the new parent, re-attach to the old one and restore the index — in that order. Run in any other one, add_child refuses a node that still has a parent and the following remove_child leaves it in no scene at all.

The effect half, and the reason this block ends in a save. Everything above was read back through the same in-memory tree the undo touched; the .tscn is where an undo that restored a node without its owner shows up as a node the editor lists and the file does not contain — the 6.1.4 failure shape exactly. It also pins the undone edits: Keeper's text is back to 'original', and Beeper left nothing behind.
A node to leave alive while its history is thrown away.

The other half of getting UndoRedo references right, and the one no undo can reach: a reference is erased together with the branch it was registered on, so a node registered on BOTH branches is freed when the history goes away even though the creation was never undone and the node is sitting in the scene. The editor discards a scene's history when the tab closes, and UndoRedo does the same to the oldest action once the tail is trimmed. is_instance_valid is asserted directly because the failure is a freed object, which every softer check reports as something else.
And it still saves: a node freed at UR-14 would leave the scene short one child here.
